title: MZ How to call on a VisuStella custom parameter?

posts.author: Allusion
rpgLord69
posts.body:
Hmmm, aren't they referenced with just the abbreviation? Like in their example 'str', so it'd be:
$gameActors.actor(1).str
Also, the way I understand it is that the value is set with the formula you give in the plugin parameters. Like the example return formula for 'str' is:
return (user.atk * 0.75) + (user.def * 0.25);
So I think you need to affect it with stuff that's in the return formula.

posts.author: Another Fen
posts.body:
I may be a bit out of the loop here. The one thing I found regarding VisuStellas menu was
this here
, which allows you to plug your own variables/parameters into the menu, but does not provide any parameter logic on its own.
Are you using this method, and if yes, how did you set up the "JS: Value" part, and if no, what are you currently using for extra parameters?
Edit
: If you are looking for a plugin to handle extra parameters,
this one
would be the first I could find. You should be able to plug in the custom parameters into VisuStellas menu by putting
return this.cparam(127);
as the "JS: Value" (replace 127 with the ID of your parameter).

posts.author: Allusion
Another Fen
posts.body:
I have not tried this myself, but from what I gathered you'd have to set your parameters up in both plugins:
You can make VisuStella mimic Elis custom parameters by giving them the same name, abbreviation, and use the code from the last post for "JS: value"
(The parameters ID is its position in Elis plugin parameter list, starting at 0)
Note: I am not 100% sure if giving the VisuStella version the same abbreviation as the Eli versions short name won't cause an error; it should be fine, but you might want to try it out first.
If the Eli-Parameter is a HP/MP/TP type parameter, then the VisuStella abbreviation should have a "max" in front of the short name as well.
To increase a parameter, you can use
$gameActors.actor(1).addCParam( ParamId , Amount );
or the corresponding plugin commands.
